Key failure: my 39/40 cluster is a pure sheep/wheat trap. Trading that cluster's surplus for brick/wood is impossible — every opponent rejected all wood->brick, wheat->sheep, etc. offers (0-for-N on offers). I ended with waste piles of wheat and nothing to build. Ash just kept converting wood via his port (4:1/2:1) and built settlements 52, 9, 25, reaching 9 VP with a city at 4.

Lessons for next match:
1. NEVER take a starting pair with only sheep/wheat production. Prioritize brick+wood clusters first, sheep/wheat second — the binding constraint in this league is brick, not wheat (many small builds need wood+brick).
2. Robber: I barely moved it (only Ash/Sail moved it). Robbing the leaders' brick/wood hexes early costs them builds; do this consistently rather than sitting on passivity.
3. Trade offers in this league almost always fail (all-reject pattern) — the port (2:1 sheep if owned) is more reliable than table offers; do not spend a turn's 3 offers hoping for acceptance.
4. Do not build roads into port-only corners (e.g. node 5 brick port was port-only, no settlement spot). Check whether a road actually opens a buildable vertex before spending wood+brick — I burned 2 roads that way.
5. Midgame: when you have a surplus of one resource and cannot build, holding 7+ cards invites discard rolls on 7. Convert surplus into development cards when sheep+wheat+ore is obtainable, or dump via port.
Assignments for future practice tables: corridor B edge [5,16]; corridor E edge [9,10]."}
